children: Shares of aerospace and defense company Hexcel
fell 12% in the morning session after the company reported third-quarter 2026 financial results, posting net sales of $496.4 million and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $0.50.

According to a company press release, Hexcel grew net sales by 8.8% year over year and saw its operating margin expand to 11%, up from 7.9% in the prior-year quarter. The company reconfirmed its full-year revenue guidance of $2.08 billion at the midpoint, reiterated its adjusted EPS outlook of $2.35 at the midpoint, and raised its share repurchase authorization to $750 million. However, quarterly revenue fell short of Wall Street's expectations of $502.8 million. In addition, the company's maintained full-year revenue guidance came in roughly 0.9% below analyst consensus estimates, and its full-year profit target also missed expectations, weighing heavily on investor sentiment.
What is the market telling us

Hexcel’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 5 moves greater than 5% over the last year. Moves this big are rare for Hexcel and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 12 months ago when the stock gained 15.2% on the news that its third-quarter 2025 earnings report presented a mixed picture that investors ultimately viewed in a positive light.

The company's revenue of $456.2 million beat Wall Street's expectations, and it generated a robust free cash flow margin of 21.2%, up significantly from 16.1% in the same quarter last year. This strong cash generation appeared to outweigh concerns from an adjusted earnings per share of $0.37 that was in line with consensus estimates. In a note of caution, Hexcel also lowered its revenue and earnings guidance for the full year, but investors seemingly focused on the quarter's top-line strength and operational cash performance.

Hexcel is up 3.2% since the beginning of the year, but at $79.37 per share, it is still trading 28% below its 52-week high of $110.28 from July 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Hexcel’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,371.
